summary: A complete target-level refinement of root Picard stacks: actual native scheme fibres and arrows, tensor/dual coherence, all integer degree components, root-frame square quotient, its relative μ₂ gerbe, the variant with a section only on R, and full inertia equations. Ordinary Picard, generic monoidal geometry, stackification and torsors are imported. Coverage is planned, not closed: exact finite-étale frame and native scheme-site integration contracts remain with their suppliers; the compact suggested file exposes only native data and coordinate milestones.

nodes.title: Native root Picard fibres and descent
nodes.statement: For i_S:R_S→X_S a root object is (L,K,ι), with L∈InvertibleSheaf(X_S), K∈InvertibleSheaf(R_S), and ι:(K⊗K).obj≅(Modules.pullback i_S).obj L.obj. An arrow to (L′,K′,ι′) is a pair of native isomorphisms (f:L≅L′,v:K≅K′) satisfying ι′∘(v⊗v)=i_S* f∘ι in R_S.Modules. Componentwise identities, composition and inverse make these a groupoid. Along S′→S pull back both lines and transport ι using the canonical tensor and pullback-composition comparisons. This defines the actual scheme-site stack refining the imported parent root-picard; its projection to the ordinary Picard stack forgets K and ι. No section of either line is part of this definition.
hypotheses: k is a field of characteristic different from 2. X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve. i:R→X is a closed immersion and R is finite étale over k, possibly empty. In the original application k is finite and R is reduced, so these hypotheses hold.

For a k-scheme S, X_S=X×_k S and R_S=R×_k S; i_S:R_S→X_S is the base change of i. All stacks use the big fppf scheme site, with the imported fpqc constructions restricted to it. Pullbacks include their identity and composition isomorphisms.

Line bundles are native TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf objects; arrows are isomorphisms, not all morphisms in that full subcategory. Tensor products are native sheaf tensor products, not tensor products of global sections.
proofSteps: Use native invertible sheaves for each object field and native module isomorphisms for ι. The arrow equation is a fixed typed equality of module morphisms. Use tensor congruence to compose and invert it; no isomorphism-class quotient is taken.

Import the coherent symmetric monoidal pullback on the native Picard core from SF.3/picard-groupoid, including its AlgebraicVectorBundles L0A/L0B dependencies. For the Cartesian base-change square, compare restriction-after-pullback and pullback-after-restriction using Modules.pullbackComp and equality of the composites.

Descend L and K by the imported effective invertible-sheaf descent. Descend ι and its invertibility by the sheaf condition for module morphisms. Descend compatible pairs of arrows by the same condition; all cocycles are retained.
acceptance: The forgetful functor has the full native ordinary Picard fibre as its codomain.
Native data and native arrow structures in the suggested file elaborate without admitted data. The groupoid and pseudofunctor instances are geometric README targets.

nodes.title: Coherent tensor product and dual of root data
nodes.statement: The native root stack is a symmetric monoidal stack of Picard groupoids. Tensor sends (L,K,ι),(M,N,κ) to (L⊗M,K⊗N, (K⊗N)²≅K²⊗N²→L|R⊗M|R≅(L⊗M)|R); the first comparison reorders the middle factors by the ordinary symmetry. The unit is (O_X,O_R,canonical O_R²≅O_X|R). The dual is (L∨,K∨, (K∨)²≅(K²)∨→(L|R)∨≅L∨|R), where the middle map is (ι∨)⁻¹. Associators, ordinary unsigned symmetry, unitors, evaluation and double dual descend from the native lines, satisfy triangle, pentagon, hexagon and inverse laws, and commute coherently with arbitrary base change and the forgetful functor. The degree grading introduces no Koszul sign.
hypotheses: k is a field of characteristic different from 2. X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve. i:R→X is a closed immersion and R is finite étale over k, possibly empty. In the original application k is finite and R is reduced, so these hypotheses hold.

For a k-scheme S, X_S=X×_k S and R_S=R×_k S; i_S:R_S→X_S is the base change of i. All stacks use the big fppf scheme site, with the imported fpqc constructions restricted to it. Pullbacks include their identity and composition isomorphisms.

Line bundles are native TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf objects; arrows are isomorphisms, not all morphisms in that full subcategory. Tensor products are native sheaf tensor products, not tensor products of global sections.
proofSteps: Import the coherent monoidal, rank-one dual and pullback interface from the native Picard groupoid supplier; do not redevelop sheaf tensor products or duals.
Define the displayed tensor square using associators and the middle-factor interchange. Apply duality to ι and invert it to obtain the correctly oriented dual comparison.

The ordinary coherence isomorphisms of both line factors satisfy the root-arrow square by naturality. Their underlying equalities prove every required root coherence diagram because an arrow is determined by its two line isomorphisms. Pullback comparisons follow the same argument.
acceptance: For a root object A, A⊗A∨ is canonically isomorphic to the root unit, with its square identification respected.
On three root objects the underlying L and K associators are the native ones; fourfold products satisfy the pentagon.
Over an odd field a degree-one object exchanged with itself has ordinary symmetry, not multiplication by −1.

sources.match: The all-degree root Picard objects support tensor translations and inverses. The explicit coherence is the categorical refinement of those operations, using the imported native Picard structure. The cited application is over a finite field; the displayed native and descent arguments justify the stated general-field, finite-étale extension.

nodes.title: Root degree components in every integer degree
nodes.statement: Define the fibrewise locally constant integer degree of (L,K,ι) to be deg(L), with no division by two. For every d∈Z, the root degree-d stack is the 2-pullback of ordinary Picard^d along forget. These open-and-closed components decompose the root stack as a coproduct indexed by Z. Tensor maps degrees (d,e) to d+e; dual maps d to −d. The decomposition commutes with arbitrary k-scheme base change. Ordinary Picard^d is imported as a G_m-gerbe over its Picard-sheaf torsor Pic^d under Pic^0. This neither chooses X(k) nor supplies a k-object in every component. Over an algebraic closure every integer component has objects.
hypotheses: k is a field of characteristic different from 2. X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve. i:R→X is a closed immersion and R is finite étale over k, possibly empty. In the original application k is finite and R is reduced, so these hypotheses hold.

Line bundles are native TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf objects; arrows are isomorphisms, not all morphisms in that full subcategory. Tensor products are native sheaf tensor products, not tensor products of global sections.
proofSteps: Import the ordinary family degree and its open-and-closed components from SF.3/picard-stack-curve, and pull those components back along forget. Families with several degrees on disconnected bases correspond to the coproduct, not to a single fixed-degree fibre.
Compute tensor and dual degree on L via the imported ordinary degree formulas. Restriction to the zero-dimensional R imposes no parity condition on this degree.

Over an algebraic closure choose a point of X to exhibit O(d x); its restriction to finite reduced R has a square root. This is a test proof of geometric nonemptiness, not a point included in the definition over k. Keep Pic^d as the supplier torsor.
acceptance: The object O(−1) in the native negative-degree test lies in component −1.
After base extension, the degree-d component is the pullback of the original degree-d component.
No equivalence Pic^d≃Pic^0 is asserted without a chosen degree-d class; no universal line is inferred from a rational point of the Picard sheaf.

sources.match: The definition ranges over all integers, and tensor translation by signed away divisors uses those components. The ordinary torsor and family-degree results are imports from SF.3. The cited application is over a finite field; the displayed native and descent arguments justify the stated general-field, finite-étale extension.

nodes.title: Root frames and the square action
nodes.statement: Import Pic_{X,R}, the groupoid of (L,γ:i_S*L≅O_RS), with arrows f satisfying γ′∘i_S*f=γ. Put T=Res_R/k G_m. For u∈T(S), set (L,γ)·u=(L,u²γ). The map to root triples sends (L,γ) to (L,O_RS,γ⁻¹), using the canonical O_RS²≅O_RS. For an intrinsic root triple, its root frames e:O_RS≅K form a T-torsor. Extract γ=(ι∘e²)⁻¹. Changing frame by e′=e∘mul(u⁻¹) changes γ to u²γ; this fixes the sign convention. This construction is natural in S, retains arrows on L, and identifies the atlas map Pic_{X,R}→RootPic with a T-torsor after every scheme base change. Rigidified line bundles themselves are imported, including the current native RigidifiedLineBundle carrier, not defined again here.
hypotheses: k is a field of characteristic different from 2. X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve. i:R→X is a closed immersion and R is finite étale over k, possibly empty. In the original application k is finite and R is reduced, so these hypotheses hold.

For a k-scheme S, X_S=X×_k S and R_S=R×_k S; i_S:R_S→X_S is the base change of i. All stacks use the big fppf scheme site, with the imported fpqc constructions restricted to it. Pullbacks include their identity and composition isomorphisms.

Line bundles are native TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf objects; arrows are isomorphisms, not all morphisms in that full subcategory. Tensor products are native sheaf tensor products, not tensor products of global sections.
proofSteps: Use the imported native rigidified-line groupoid along i_S. Finite-étale Weil restriction supplies the frame functor and T, with arbitrary base-change compatibility; this is the precise GC0-WEIL-FRAMES request.
Over a frame, apply ι to e² and invert to extract γ. Compare e and e′ to obtain the formula γ′=u²γ, including its identity and product laws.

For a map S→RootPic, objects of the 2-fibre product with Pic_{X,R} are rigidified lines together with a specified root isomorphism to the given triple. Sending this datum to its induced frame gives the frame torsor, including its arrows; the inverse uses that frame. Descent supplies frames locally even when K is not globally trivial.
acceptance: The ordinary rigidification-change action without squaring would lose the relative μ₂ stabilizer.
The inverse square orientation is fixed by γ:L|R→O: (u²γ)⁻¹ u²=γ⁻¹.
A finite non-split R is treated by restriction of scalars and not by a chosen list of k-points.

nodes.title: Square quotient equivalence on objects and arrows
nodes.statement: The root-frame atlas induces a base-change-compatible equivalence [Pic_{X,R}/T]≃RootPic_{X,R}, where T acts by γ↦u²γ. The quotient means the stackification of the action groupoid, equivalently T-torsors with equivariant maps to the rigidified Picard stack, with full descent isomorphisms. The equivalence commutes with the map to the ordinary Picard stack and restricts to every d∈Z. On the atlas it is the stated (L,O,γ⁻¹) functor; on a change by u its root isomorphism is (1,u). The inverse uses the torsor of actual root-line frames, with unit and counit recovered by descent of the frame identification. For nonempty R the rigidified Picard stack has trivial inertia and is an algebraic space; SF.3 ordinary Picard algebraicity and SF.1 quotient algebraicity give algebraicity of RootPic. For empty R the statement reduces to the ordinary Picard stack, without treating it as an algebraic space.
hypotheses: k is a field of characteristic different from 2. X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve. i:R→X is a closed immersion and R is finite étale over k, possibly empty. In the original application k is finite and R is reduced, so these hypotheses hold.

For a k-scheme S, X_S=X×_k S and R_S=R×_k S; i_S:R_S→X_S is the base change of i. All stacks use the big fppf scheme site, with the imported fpqc constructions restricted to it. Pullbacks include their identity and composition isomorphisms.

Line bundles are native TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf objects; arrows are isomorphisms, not all morphisms in that full subcategory. Tensor products are native sheaf tensor products, not tensor products of global sections.
proofSteps: The arrow (1,u) satisfies the square by (u²γ)⁻¹u²=γ⁻¹, so the atlas functor is equivariant with the specified comparison and cocycle.
Identify its 2-kernel pair with the T-action groupoid using the frame torsor. Apply the imported quotient stackification universal property to obtain the comparison.

An intrinsic root triple supplies its frame torsor and equivariant rigidification. The local frame identifications descend to the counit; reconstructing the same frame torsor gives the unit. Check both triangle identities on the covering torsor, then descend. This proves full faithfulness as well as local essential surjectivity.

For algebraicity, the frame morphism over the ordinary algebraic Picard stack is representable by finite-étale restriction of line-frame spaces. If R≠∅, an automorphism of L trivial on R is the identity because Γ(X_S,O)=Γ(S,O) universally and R_S→S is faithfully flat. Thus Pic_{X,R} is an algebraic space. Apply the imported smooth-T quotient theorem; handle R=∅ separately.
acceptance: The equivalence identifies full arrow groupoids, not just isomorphism classes.
The nontrivial root-line example is in its essential image through a nontrivial frame torsor.
Its composite with forget is the usual quotient induced by square T→T, not a map discarding ordinary scalar arrows.

sources.match: The square-action quotient statement is implemented through the intrinsic root frames; its descent and full-arrow form are the needed refinement. The cited application is over a finite field; the displayed native and descent arguments justify the stated general-field, finite-étale extension.

nodes.title: The forgetful root gerbe and its band
nodes.statement: The forgetful morphism RootPic_{X,R}→Pic_X is a gerbe banded by H=Res_R/k μ₂, compatibly with arbitrary scheme base change and degree components. For a fixed L on X_S, the 2-fibre is the groupoid of (K,ι:K²≅L_R); its arrows act over the identity of L. For every such object, relative automorphisms are exactly units u on R_S with u²=1. Root objects exist fppf-locally, and any two are locally isomorphic. A chosen root trivializes this gerbe as BH_S; no canonical global root or product splitting is asserted. H is finite étale of rank 2^ρ for ρ=rank(R/k). Over an algebraic closure with r branch points the relative inertia is μ₂^r. The entire root stack has the ordinary scalar automorphisms in addition, as the full-stabilizer theorem specifies.
hypotheses: k is a field of characteristic different from 2. X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve. i:R→X is a closed immersion and R is finite étale over k, possibly empty. In the original application k is finite and R is reduced, so these hypotheses hold.

For a k-scheme S, X_S=X×_k S and R_S=R×_k S; i_S:R_S→X_S is the base change of i. All stacks use the big fppf scheme site, with the imported fpqc constructions restricted to it. Pullbacks include their identity and composition isomorphisms.

Line bundles are native TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf objects; arrows are isomorphisms, not all morphisms in that full subcategory. Tensor products are native sheaf tensor products, not tensor products of global sections.
proofSteps: In the 2-fibre over L include a specified identification of the underlying line with L, so the root-arrow equation is over the identity, not an unrestricted scalar on L.

Finite-étale-locally split R_S and trivialize L_R; trivial lines then give a local root. Isomorphisms between two roots are locally frames with a prescribed square, and the n=2 Kummer epimorphism supplies them.

The same arrow square identifies every relative automorphism with a unit on R_S whose square is one. Finite-étale restriction of scalars gives H and all base-change comparisons. Composition is unit multiplication, which is commutative, so it supplies the canonical band.

Choose one root only to describe the equivalence with H-torsors: send another root to the sheaf of root isomorphisms from the chosen one, and descend the inverse twist. This is a conditional neutrality statement.
acceptance: At R=∅ the band is trivial and forget is an equivalence.

Over F₅, with R a rational point and L=O fixed, root identifications 1 and 2 are not isomorphic over that fixed L: 2 is not a square. They become isomorphic after a quadratic extension; being a gerbe is a local assertion.
For nonempty R, μ₂ relative inertia prevents the forgetful morphism from being representable by algebraic spaces.

nodes.title: Native root data with a section only on R
nodes.statement: The root-section fibre has objects (A,α) where A=(L,K,ι) is a native root object and α∈Γ(R_S,K); arrows are root arrows (f,v) with v(α)=α′. There is no section a of L on X_S and no equation against a|R. This is the native RootPicardSectionData i_S and its displayed Iso type, organized into an fppf stack using the native section pullback and descent. Forgetting α is a morphism to RootPic and has the zero-section right inverse. The squared evaluation is ι(α⊗α)∈Γ(R_S,L_R), using the imported native tensorSection operation; it need not extend to X_S. Tensor sends (A,α),(B,β) to (A⊗B,α⊗β), making a commutative monoid stack with unit section 1. The zero-section object is not tensor-invertible when R_S≠∅. On the empty R_S even its zero section is a frame. The tensor-invertible objects are exactly those with α a frame of K.

nodes.title: The section quotient and affine root-section charts
nodes.statement: Let V=Res_R/k A¹, with T-action a↦u a. Then RootPicSection≃[(Pic_{X,R}×V)/T] for the diagonal right action (γ,a)·u=(u²γ,u a). On the atlas this sends (L,γ,a) to (L,O,γ⁻¹,a); forgetting a is the square quotient comparison, and a=0 is the zero section. In frames the squared evaluation has coordinate γ⁻¹ a² in L_R, unchanged by (γ,a)↦(u²γ,u a). The forgetful map RootPicSection→RootPic is representable and affine, fppf-locally the projection A^ρ→S obtained by trivializing the actual K on the finite-étale R_S. Its zero section is a closed immersion. The comparison and all these maps commute with arbitrary base change and every integer degree.
hypotheses: k is a field of characteristic different from 2. X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve. i:R→X is a closed immersion and R is finite étale over k, possibly empty. In the original application k is finite and R is reduced, so these hypotheses hold.

For a k-scheme S, X_S=X×_k S and R_S=R×_k S; i_S:R_S→X_S is the base change of i. All stacks use the big fppf scheme site, with the imported fpqc constructions restricted to it. Pullbacks include their identity and composition isomorphisms.

Line bundles are native TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf objects; arrows are isomorphisms, not all morphisms in that full subcategory. Tensor products are native sheaf tensor products, not tensor products of global sections.
proofSteps: In a root frame e write α=e(a). With e′=e u⁻¹, its coordinate is a′=u a while γ′=u²γ. These formulas supply an equivariant atlas functor with the same root comparison (1,u).
Apply the same frame-torsor descent inverse as in square-quotient-comparison, now retaining the equivariant coordinate a. Unit and counit preserve α because they are induced by its actual frames.

For a fixed root object over S, its 2-fibre of sections is the sheaf S′↦Γ(R_S′,K_S′), not a quotient by root automorphisms. Split R and frame K locally to identify it with A^ρ. The transition maps are invertible linear maps, so the affine schemes and zero sections descend by SF.1/affine-fpqc-descent.
Use the square/weight-one identity to check squared evaluation and the compatibility of both forgetting maps. Since all formulas are on R_S, they add no global section to L.
acceptance: Over one split branch point and F₅, (γ,a)=(1,1) and u=2 yield (4,2). Both have squared evaluation 1, since 4⁻¹·2²=1.
At a=0 the relative μ₂ inertia survives; at a frame it is killed. Thus the section variant is not uniformly the same μ₂-gerbe over ordinary Pic_X.
When R=∅, V is the final scheme and the section quotient is the ordinary Picard stack.

sources.match: The associated quotient uses the square action on the rigidification and the dilation action on the root-section coordinate. Its affine chart is descent of those actual root sections. nodes.title: Full and relative inertia, including root sections
nodes.statement: For any root object over S, its full automorphism sheaf consists of c∈Γ(S,O_S)× and u∈Γ(R_S,O_RS)× satisfying u²=c|R_S; here c acts on L via the universal identity Γ(X_S,O)=Γ(S,O). Relative to a fixed L and its identity, impose c=1, giving Res μ₂. With root section α, add uα=α. These are equalities of sheaves on every S′→S, including nonreduced S′. After base change to an algebraically closed field with r branch points and compatible frames, full inertia is {(c,u_1,…,u_r):u_j²=c}, and the section inertia additionally has u_j a_j=a_j. Relative section inertia is μ₂ on exactly the zero coordinates and trivial on nonzero coordinates over that field. If any a_j≠0 then c=1 in the full section inertia; if r>0 and every coordinate is nonzero the full section inertia is trivial. For r=0 the full inertia remains G_m, while relative inertia is trivial.
hypotheses: k is a field of characteristic different from 2. X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve. i:R→X is a closed immersion and R is finite étale over k, possibly empty. In the original application k is finite and R is reduced, so these hypotheses hold.

For a k-scheme S, X_S=X×_k S and R_S=R×_k S; i_S:R_S→X_S is the base change of i. All stacks use the big fppf scheme site, with the imported fpqc constructions restricted to it. Pullbacks include their identity and composition isomorphisms.

Line bundles are native TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf objects; arrows are isomorphisms, not all morphisms in that full subcategory. Tensor products are native sheaf tensor products, not tensor products of global sections.
proofSteps: An automorphism of an invertible sheaf is multiplication by a unique unit. The imported universal global-functions identity for X_S identifies the unit on L with c from S; the root line has unit u on R_S.
Translate the root-arrow square to u²=c|R. Translate preservation of α to uα=α. These equations are functorial on all S′, so they compute group sheaves, not only geometric point groups.

Set c=1 for relative inertia. In split geometric coordinates, a nonzero field element cancels in u_j a_j=a_j, forcing u_j=1 and c=1 if any such coordinate exists. Do not cancel α over arbitrary rings; retain the equations there.
acceptance: With one split branch point, full root inertia is G_m via u↦(u²,u), whereas relative inertia is μ₂.
Over F₅ at α=0, u=−1 is a relative automorphism; at α=1 it is not.
For r=2 and α=(1,0), the full section inertia is μ₂ on the second coordinate. At α=(0,0) it also contains varying c.
Over F₅[ε]/(ε²) with α=ε, the equations apply without declaring α zero because α²=0: u=−1 does not fix α, since −ε≠ε.

For r=0, all section-coordinate equations are vacuous and the full inertia is G_m. The coordinate full-triviality milestone explicitly assumes r>0, while the relative frame-stabilizer milestone needs no nonempty-index assumption.

importedParentTargets.title: The graded root Picard stack
importedParentTargets.statement: Pic_X^√R(S) is the groupoid of (L,K_R,ι), where L is a line bundle on X×S, K_R a line bundle on R×S and ι:K_R²≅L|_{R×S}. Its degree-d component imposes degree d on every geometric fibre; d ranges over all integers. Tensor product and dual give the graded commutative Picard stack.
